latest_analysis.summary: These sample records suggest that fundraising success and community value need separate measures. The dinner generated the highest recorded net proceeds, while the walk combined strong fundraising efficiency with documented resource engagement. Recurring operational risks involved food costs, volunteer meals, late printing, program length, and preparation. Preserve welcoming activities and meaningful conversation while tightening budgets, vendor terms, payment collection, and accessibility planning. All findings are illustrative because every event is marked as demo data.

lessons.theme: Define success before selecting a format
lessons.text: From the Campus Wellness Panel and Butterfly Benefit Dinner: distinguish awareness, fundraising, and community objectives before choosing a format. Apply the board's already-adopted event-purpose recommendation rather than treating fundraising totals as the sole measure of success.

themes.name: Fundraising purpose and format
themes.description: The dinner led recorded net proceeds, but the panel's awareness purpose was not aligned with its fundraising expectations. The board has already adopted a recommendation to agree on event purpose before evaluating format and spending.

themes.name: Food costs and volunteer meals
themes.description: Walk and dinner reflections report food overruns, vendor minimums, and volunteers going short of food. Board members differ on whether the dinner meal is primarily a budget risk or an essential part of donor care.

themes.name: Volunteer preparation
themes.description: The walk's volunteer structure and dinner check-in team were praised, while raffle volunteers lacked clear roles when the event began.

themes.name: Sponsorship and production deadlines
themes.description: Sponsors provided water, shirts, table support, and raffle prizes. Late sponsor artwork and last-minute printing created avoidable complications.

themes.name: Connection through purposeful activities
themes.description: Resource tables, a recovery speaker, peer panelists, mental-health trivia, and a welcome table supported reported conversation, welcome, or engagement. Most evidence is board observation or reported attendee feedback rather than verified belonging outcomes.

themes.name: Access and event pacing
themes.description: Records describe insufficient shade and water, entrance steps, difficulty hearing a speaker, requests for quiet conversation space, and programs or draws that ran too long.
